item.title: A strong El Niño actually means fewer Atlantic hurricanes, but the Pacific has been extra stormy
item.description: While the Central and Eastern Pacific have seen 16 named storms, no Atlantic hurricane has formed so far this season. Here’s why. The Atlantic Ocean has had an unusually quiet hurricane season this year. Though there have been six named storms, zero have actually strengthened into hurricanes—a rarity that hasn’t occurred in decades.
